speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any fever?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The weight loss of twelve pounds is significant; have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea, constipation, or blood in your stool? Additionally, have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or a lump in your throat?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma. The combination of significant weight loss, night sweats, fatigue, abdominal pain, and a fixed, painless supraclavicular lymph node is highly suggestive of malignancy, specifically lymphoma. Please undergo an urgent biopsy of the lymph node and a CT scan of the abdomen and chest. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy; REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis
